name: United Arab Emirates

facts.religion: Muslim about 75%, Christian and Hindu expatriate communities

system_note: A federation of seven hereditary monarchies.
snapshot: Iran fired more missiles and drones at the UAE than at any other country, hitting Dubai landmarks and shaking the region's safe-harbour reputation.
culture: In half a century the Emirates went from pearl-diving villages to a global crossroads; around nine in ten residents are foreigners, and Dubai's malls, the Burj Khalifa and Abu Dhabi's Louvre symbolise the transformation. Emirati culture keeps falconry, camel racing and the kandura and abaya dress. The UAE has promoted itself as a hub for religious tolerance, building the Abrahamic Family House.
society: Oil wealth, concentrated in Abu Dhabi, funds the federation, while Dubai lives from trade, aviation, property and tourism. The UAE has invested heavily in AI, space and renewable energy. Political parties are banned and critics jailed. It normalised ties with Israel in 2020 and has backed forces in Sudan, Libya and Yemen.
situation: In 1971 seven sheikhdoms on a desert coast joined into a federation. Fifty years later Dubai and Abu Dhabi had become the Middle East's financial capital, its busiest airport and one of the world's great playgrounds, the region's safe harbour. The 2026 war tested that reputation directly.

When Iran retaliated for the US-Israeli strikes, the UAE became its main target: by June Iran had fired more than 1,900 missiles and drones at it, more than at any other country (AFP via Oman Observer). Most were shot down, but debris and strikes hit Al Dhafra air base, the Burj Al Arab hotel, a Dubai Marina tower, the oil refinery at Fujairah and fuel tanks near Dubai airport, which closed and partially reopened on 7 March (Arab News). By late June eight people had died. More than $120 billion was wiped off the Dubai and Abu Dhabi stock markets within weeks (Middle East Eye via Spill). President Mohammed bin Zayed told the nation, "We are in a period of war, but we will emerge stronger." One asset proved its worth: a pipeline from Habshan to Fujairah lets much of the UAE's oil bypass the closed Strait of Hormuz. The war also exposed a rift with Saudi Arabia: in January Riyadh drove the UAE-backed separatists out of southern Yemen, and Abu Dhabi withdrew its forces. The UAE also faces accusations, which it denies, of arming Sudan's RSF.
power: A federation of seven hereditary monarchies. The rulers form the Supreme Council, which elects the president, by custom the ruler of Abu Dhabi; the ruler of Dubai is vice president and prime minister. The Federal National Council is advisory, half elected by a limited electorate.
holders: President Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan; Vice President and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum.

update.html: On 9 October a laden supertanker anchored about 13 nautical miles off the UAE coast was hit by an unidentified projectile amid a wave of attacks on Gulf shipping. Oil from the tanker reached the shore, and on 23 October the environment ministry closed all beaches in Umm Al Quwain.
